task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

historical_evidence.finding: Pre-game PT PPP ranking from training data correlates with actual efficiency ranking in held-out games; median rho +0.539, 90.8% positive lift; 10.5% rows mislead (rho<0). Auto_has_risk: RISK:DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY.
PNR shot-level season rates vary by team: OKC 7.567%, BOS 7.854%, IND 13.824%, NYK 11.959%, ATL 11.361%, DEN 11.404%, PHX 10.232%. Rates are calibration input for PBPProxyPNR.
TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games; small team-PT lifts, large player-channel lifts on small n; limited exposure.
Defensive PPP allowed and possession share, RS vs playoffs: DRIVE allowed 1.191→0.923, share 21.2%→18.2%; PNR -0.139, share +12.1pp; PULL_UP +0.341, share -7.6pp.

failed_approaches.what_failed: TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games

evidence_establishes: Baseline PNR share rates vary by team; pull-up share differences between regular season and playoffs; some evidence of lift in holdout play-type validation (but not specific to PNR fail).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether pull-up after a PNR fail produces lift>0 in >=70% of units; median lift>2pp; causal relationship; effect size; sample size adequacy; measurement reliability of PNR fail and pull-up labels.
own_inferences: The available data provide descriptive rates but lack a clear counterfactual design to isolate the effect of pull-up following a PNR failure. The question as posed requires defining PNR fail and pull-up at the possession level and sufficient exposure to estimate lift.
uncertainties: Definition and labeling of PNR fail and pull-up events; exposure sparsity of PNR fail; potential confounding by defensive matchups and game context; measurement reliability of possession-level tags; season-to-season drift.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved studies did not answer the specific lift question; they provide baseline rates and some validation but not the causal effect after PNR fail. Therefore the decision remains unchanged.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR fail events are rare, limiting power.
Uncertain reliability of PNR fail and pull-up labeling.
Minimal detectable effect size may exceed 2pp in many units.
Seasonal changes in play style could bias results.
Defensive matchups, tempo, and game context may confound lift estimates.

prior_work.summary: Prior work has quantified PNR share rates and pull-up shares and validated play-type ranking, but has not directly tested the lift of pull-up after a PNR failure at the league-wide level.

risks.text: Limited number of PNR failure events per unit.
Potential mislabeling of PNR failure and pull-up events.
Effect size threshold may be too low to detect with available data.
Season-to-season changes in play style or rules.
Defensive matchups, tempo, and other contextual factors.

design.estimand: Difference in points per 100 possessions for pull-up attempts following a PNR failure versus pull-up attempts following a successful PNR or other contexts
design.sample: All team-games with at least 5 PNR failure events and at least 10 pull-up attempts in the same game
design.power: Estimated via simulation assuming 2pp effect and 70% units with positive lift; requires ~200 team-games with sufficient events
design.controls: Opponent defensive rating, pace, player availability, and game situation (score differential)
design.falsification: Test lift for random periods of the game and for pull-up attempts following non-PNR events
design.multiplicity: Adjust for multiple units using Holm-Bonferroni; report effect size distribution
design.decision_rule: Reject null if ≥70% of units show lift>0 with median lift>2pp, after controlling for covariates
design.data_version: NBA 2025-26 regular season up to 2026-04-13, including playoffs up to 2026-06-21
